categories.justification: Answers the actual decision and covers all three mustFlag issues: the Enterprise requirement, the undocumented private connectivity, and Brickwork being cheaper. It also covers capacity, growth, billing definitions, audit-log coverage and contract questions, with no irrelevant padding.
quotes: Formline only offers those on its Enterprise plan, which costs **$9,500/month**.
Formline may fail the private-database requirement on any plan.
Brickwork is the only option that meets all three mandatory requirements on paper.

categories.justification: Every number I checked is correct: $6,600, $8,850, the 593 break-even, 43.9%, the 2-year totals of $185,400 vs $228,000, and the 20-builder break-even of about 567. It also confirms IT's 27.3% arithmetic while correctly saying the wrong plan was compared. Nothing appears fabricated, and the web search that found no independent source is disclosed.
quotes: With 12 builders, that happens at about **593 end users**.

categories.justification: Explains why an IP allowlist cannot reach a database with no public IP, and quantifies break-even, 2-year total cost and when the Team plan's user cap is hit. It analyses failure modes specific to this case: billing definitions, the Relay agent as a single point of failure, and whether audit logs cover data changes.
quotes: An IP allowlist only controls who may connect to an address that is already reachable from the internet.
If there is only one Relay instance, all 30 tools that use on-prem data go down when it does.
If builders do count toward the cap, you would reach 500 at about 488 end users, roughly 14 months in at linear growth.

categories.justification: Challenges IT's framing directly and presents fair counterarguments (flat pricing, a possible Formline private option, negotiation). It also states what would change the conclusion, such as the discount Formline would need and the growth thresholds.
quotes: The sums are correct; the plan they compare is not
It would need to come down by more than about 30%, to below $6,600, to beat Brickwork today.
Re-open Formline only if it can show a supported private connectivity option and a price that beats Brickwork.

categories.justification: Gives a clear bottom line with conditions, specific questions for each vendor, a proof of concept, and contract actions.
quotes: Do not sign the Formline Team plan. Treat Brickwork as the provisional front-runner.
Is there any supported way to reach a database with no public IP (an agent, VPN, PrivateLink-style link, self-hosted option)?
Run a short proof of concept with Brickwork Relay against the real database.

categories.justification: Well organised, with calculations shown and uncertainty labelled explicitly. However, several material claims, such as the user caps of 500 and 1,000 and the 550-user growth projection, are not tied to a specific source file.

mustFlagAdjudication.quote: Formline only offers those on its Enterprise plan, which costs **$9,500/month**.
Private connection to Postgres with no public IP (mandatory) | **Not documented.**

notesForHumanAdjudicator: I checked all arithmetic independently and it is correct. I could not verify three details against the supplied documents because the packet only names them: the Formline user caps (Team 500, Enterprise 1,000), the 550-end-user growth projection, and the quoted vendor wording. They agree with the reference where it overlaps. The output frames the gap as Formline being 44% more expensive, while the reference frames it as Brickwork being about 30% cheaper. These are the same figures expressed two ways, and the output also gives the 30% figure. None of the mustNotClaim patterns appear.
